Summary

61 minima and 127 transition states from 1 input structure(s) in 500 job(s); 347 warning(s); 61 minima and 127 transition states or crossing points are shown; 13 path peak(s) (the highest points of paths that gave no verified transition state) are saved in path_peaks.csv and are no part of the network. Energies relative to the lowest minimum, in kcal/mol; populations by Boltzmann at 298.15 K of the energies of the minima shown (not all have a free energy).

Evaluations of the run: 342926 gradient calculation(s), 24452 exact Hessian calculation(s); no microiterations (no ONIOM environment was relaxed).

Every structure at its place by classical multidimensional scaling of all 188 structures of the mass-weighted distances between the structures (ReSPer; any two of the first four principal coordinates, in Å amu1/2, on one scale): minima as circles (the lowest ringed), transition states as diamonds, each link from its two minima through its transition state; colors by relative energy. Distances between permuted atoms are not reduced, so equivalent structures with other atom numbers lie apart. Drag to move, Ctrl + wheel or the buttons to zoom, double-click to fit.

Graph

The minima as nodes, each link (transition state, diamond) as an edge between its two minima; the places are a force-directed layout of the links (Fruchterman and Reingold 1991), the lowest minima in the middle; distances on the page mean nothing more. Drag a minimum to move it (its transition states follow), drag elsewhere to move the view, Ctrl + wheel or the buttons to zoom, double-click to fit.

This figure needs scripts.

The minima on a circle and every link as a chord through its transition state. With a lowest-barrier path chosen (below, or with the buttons “Chosen node as start” and “Chosen node as end”), its start is at the left, its end at the right and its minima in their order along the upper half; the other minima are along the lower half, each under the minimum of the path it is joined to in the fewest steps. Without a path the minima follow round the circle in the order of their steps from the lowest minimum. With a species chosen, the circle holds its conformers alone. “A circle per species” draws every species as a circle of its conformers, the circles round a ring, and the links between two species as lines from circle to circle.

Chemical species

The minima shown grouped by their SMILES strings: minima with one string are conformers of one species. The strings are written from the structures (bonds from the covalent radii, bond orders from the usual valences, @ and @@ at tetrahedral centres of four different substituents, rings in a Kekule form): R and S are two species, / and \ about a double bond outside the rings make E and Z two species, and a bond order is a guess where the valence rules do not hold.
